title: Design the room
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What does the room say before you speak?
I said I want to control a little the environment, not only what I say and the dialogue, but whether it is a loud or a quiet place, whether you can hear traffic, whether the music is loud.
A student described a tense environment: everyone is on edge, there is a lot at stake and everybody feels it.

I said that you can create an environment that starts with soft music barely heard in the background, and maybe fresh flowers, and that you should be aware of anything that creates friction before you say anything.
Another said that in virtual meetings you cannot let others sense the scent or the music, so it is more about the energy.
I said to ask someone: what is something you like about me that you would like me to keep doing? I said it is a powerful question, not shallow praise.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the places where you meet people.
Write what is loud, bright or tense there.
Write what you would add: sound, scent, light.
Write the question you will ask.

check.q: What did I say I control a little?
choices: The environment as well as the words

check.q: What did I say to look for before you speak?

choices: What do you like me to keep doing

recap: Design the room. Remove friction. Ask what to keep.
